route_status.proven_scope: The exact Godot 4.7.2.stable scripted probe passed in Classic mode: primary finger drag steered; second-finger tap jumped; second-finger drag changed camera without jumping; camera returned after lift; a 300 ms still hold became held jump and release cleared it; focus loss cleared touch state; and the Galaxy camera responded to touch. Receipt: runtime/L35/attempt_1/receipt.json (exit 0, no failure lines, headless, isolated profile); runtime/L35/attempt_1/probe.log records these PASS lines.
route_status.route_gaps: This is not a normal child-visible route. The probe skips the intro, forces Classic with main._set_touch_mode("classic", false), sends synthetic coordinates, and directly starts Galaxy. The shipping/default mode is Hybrid (scripts/main.gd:609-611); the probe does not exercise that mode's movement-zone ownership or show the initial display. No GUI/Mobile render, physical phone, child, or owner session was observed.

code_constants.value: Stick radius R = 78 px; movement begins after TAP_SLOP = 22 px, and stick magnitude scales from that slop to the radius.
code_constants.scope: Source-defined Classic/Hybrid gesture thresholds; physical touch comfort and rendered response are unmeasured.

code_constants.value: Classic still-finger classification threshold is JUMP_HOLD_MS = 140 ms; the probe waits 300 ms for its held-jump assertion and up to 3000 ms for camera drift-back.
code_constants.scope: Code and probe synchronization only. The helper's 17.484 seconds is execution time, not play duration.

timing.assumptions: No child session length or perceived delay inferred from headless frame waits or runner wall time.

tactile.target_size: Hybrid movement_zone() spans x=0 to max(390, 34% of viewport width) and y=52%-100% of viewport height (scripts/touch_ui.gd:315-323). At 1280x720 that is approximately 435x346 canvas pixels. It is a large claimed region, but no rendered/physical target size or device projection was measured.
tactile.press_response: In Hybrid, a press in movement_zone() is assigned STICK and passed to _press(); _press() hides the base and knob and zeros stick_vec, then _drag() steers after movement exceeds 22 px (scripts/touch_ui.gd:688-697, 197-229, 237-247). No rendered-frame or real-device latency was measured.
tactile.drag_hold_release: The probe drove a 60 px primary-finger movement, a second-finger camera drag, a 300 ms still hold, and release; it confirms Classic behavior only (scripts/probe_touch_look.gd:40-47, 60-85, 87-102). Hybrid physical drag/hold/release feel was not observed.
tactile.ownership: The scripted probe's Classic interactions pass, but it establishes no child route. Hybrid assigns a lower-left press to STICK before the direct-world owner branch while no movement pad is visible (scripts/touch_ui.gd:688-706, 299-307, 315-323).
tactile.cancellation: The probe directly sends NOTIFICATION_APPLICATION_FOCUS_OUT and confirms stick/action/look state clears (scripts/probe_touch_look.gd:104-115; runtime/L35/attempt_1/probe.log). This is a scripted notification assertion, not native OS focus-loss behavior.

play_appeal.agency: Hypothesis: once a child discovers the lower-left drag, direction-matched steering can feel direct because the stick origin follows the finger (scripts/touch_ui.gd:197-210). The hidden Hybrid region may instead make the first drag feel unexplained; neither response was observed from a child.
play_appeal.variety: The tested Classic route gives a second finger separate tap/jump and drag/look roles, with hold and release states. The default Hybrid movement/world-tap path was not tested here.
play_appeal.world_response: Classic probe assertions show steering, camera orbit/return, held jump/release and focus cleanup in state. They do not establish that these responses are visibly legible in a rendered phone session.
play_appeal.replay: Not assessed for this touch-control focus.
play_appeal.appeal_test: On the exact rendered phone build in default Hybrid mode, offer a fresh child the game without naming any control region; record whether they discover movement independently, whether initial presses visibly explain what happened, and whether a painted object in the lower-left bay can still be selected. Compare the same sequence with a visible movement cue, without treating the comparison as acceptance until owner/device/child gates are completed.

observations.title: Default Hybrid silently assigns a large hidden lower-left movement bay
evidence: scripts/main.gd:609-611 sets the initial mode to TOUCH_MODE_HYBRID.
scripts/touch_ui.gd:315-323 defines the lower-left movement zone; :688-706 assigns a press inside it to STICK before the world-interaction route.
scripts/touch_ui.gd:104-114 creates the explanatory ghost wheel with visible=false; :197-229 hides the stick base and knob on press; :299-307 hides all three indicators at rest.

scripts/touch_ui.gd:202-205 documents that the claimed region previously shoved Roshan right with nothing on screen; the current finger anchoring fixes direction consistency but leaves the region hidden.
observations.reproduction: On the default Hybrid code path, press within the lower-left movement_zone (for example, the 1280x720 canvas point (100, 500)), then drag more than 22 px. The input router assigns STICK ownership; the hint, base, and knob remain hidden. The precise screen outcome requires rendered/device reproduction; this source trace is not a claimed live touch observation.
observations.child_impact: A non-reader can encounter an unmarked movement-only region and receive no visible control explanation at touch-down. A child trying to tap an object there may instead begin steering, making the world feel inconsistent or dependent on adult instruction.
observations.proposed_repair: Treat as a candidate source defect for the coordinator to reproduce. Align the Hybrid ownership region with DL-UI-02: either make its movement affordance visible and clear when needed, or stop silently reserving the hidden region for movement while preserving the direct-touch grammar.
observations.acceptance_test: In the actual Mobile-rendered default Hybrid route, inspect the full screen at supported aspects and verify every movement-owned region has a visible, child-legible affordance before and during touch, or that world targets remain directly selectable there. A first-time child should independently discover steering without text or adult direction; retain routed touch traces and owner/device review.

observations.title: L35's green probe covers forced Classic gestures rather than default Hybrid discoverability
evidence: scripts/probe_touch_look.gd:36-38 explicitly says Hybrid/world taps are covered elsewhere and calls main._set_touch_mode("classic", false).

observations.acceptance_test: Keep the exact Classic assertions green and add a routed Hybrid trace that checks first press/drag ownership at bay boundaries, visible feedback, competing world taps, and release. Pair it with Mobile captures and a separate unprompted child observation.

observations.title: Classic gesture mechanics have positive scripted state evidence
evidence: audit/cycles/luna-playtest-20261012/runtime/L35/attempt_1/probe.log: PASS stick steers; PASS second-finger tap jumps; PASS second-finger drag drives camera, no jump; PASS drifts back after camera finger lifts; PASS still hold becomes HELD jump; PASS held jump releases; PASS focus loss clears touch state; PASS galaxy touch camera works.
scripts/probe_touch_look.gd:40-74 exercises primary stick, secondary tap and secondary drag; :77-102 checks camera return and hold/release; :104-139 checks focus-loss and Galaxy camera touch.
observations.reproduction: The exact-run receipt names Godot 4.7.2.stable.official.ed1daf0bf, frozen baseline e2b3c73789707aa49a91b4f42e2a9dd4b68225df, exit code 0, and no failure lines; the retained probe log includes each stated PASS assertion.
observations.child_impact: The code-level gesture paths have deterministic positive checks for split roles and cleanup, reducing risk of stuck scripted state. This does not show that a child knows to use a second finger or likes the interaction.
observations.proposed_repair: Preserve this passing Classic coverage while evaluating the default Hybrid affordance separately; do not infer a visible child-facing control from state assertions.
observations.acceptance_test: Replay the exact Classic probe unchanged and retain its PASS receipt; independently verify one-finger first-use Hybrid play on device with no stuck state, unintended world-selection loss, or adult prompt.

strengths.claim: Classic gesture paths have focused automated evidence for steering, jump tap/hold/release, camera drag/return, focus cleanup, and Galaxy camera movement.
strengths.evidence: audit/cycles/luna-playtest-20261012/runtime/L35/attempt_1/probe.log and scripts/probe_touch_look.gd:40-139; this proves scripted Classic assertions only.

strengths.claim: The stick origin follows the finger, avoiding the previously documented direction mismatch from an invisible fixed anchor.
strengths.evidence: scripts/touch_ui.gd:197-210; source comment records prior lower-left/rightward mismatch at :199-205. No physical touch feel was evaluated.

acceptance_gaps: Default Hybrid ownership and hidden-region boundary have no L35 routed-input assertion; L35 explicitly switches to Classic.
No Mobile-rendered capture confirms indicator visibility, canvas projection, or world-object selection around the lower-left bay.
No target-phone measurement establishes physical hit comfort, touch latency, native focus-loss behavior, or frame pacing.
No observed child evidence establishes non-reader discovery, comprehension, comfort, appeal, or independent play; owner acceptance is also pending.

play_sequence.beat: The probe instantiates main.tscn, waits one process frame, calls _skip_intro(), waits 20 more process frames, then forces Classic mode; this is setup, not normal entry.
play_sequence.inputs_and_waits: One await process_frame; then 20 await process_frame iterations; then _set_touch_mode("classic", false).

play_sequence.beat: Finger 0 tests movement: press at (400,700), drag to (460,700), wait one process frame, and check stick magnitude >=0.3.
play_sequence.inputs_and_waits: 60 px drag; one process frame before the state assertion.

play_sequence.beat: Finger 1 tests a tap while finger 0 owns the stick: tap at (1200,700), wait one frame after down and one after up, then consume the jump edge.
play_sequence.inputs_and_waits: Finger 1 down (1200,700); await process_frame; up at same point; await process_frame.

play_sequence.beat: Finger 1 tests camera peek: drag from (1200,700) through 12 points, each (+40,-8) from the prior point, awaiting one frame per move; lift and allow drift-back check up to 3000 ms.
play_sequence.inputs_and_waits: 12 frame-spaced drags (total +480,-96 px); after lift, wall-clock loop until 3000 ms or check passes.

play_sequence.beat: A separate still finger 1 press at (1300,800) waits 300 ms to check held jump, then lifts and waits one frame to verify release clears it.
play_sequence.inputs_and_waits: 300 ms wall-clock hold; release; one process frame.

play_sequence.beat: Focus-loss cleanup starts finger 0 steering plus finger 1 hold, waits one frame, sends NOTIFICATION_APPLICATION_FOCUS_OUT, waits one more frame, and checks all active touch state cleared.
play_sequence.inputs_and_waits: Two fingers; one frame before and one frame after direct focus-loss notification.

play_sequence.beat: The probe starts Galaxy directly, waits 30 process frames, then repeats finger 0 steering and a finger 1 drag over 12 frame-spaced moves of +40 px each; orbit must exceed 0.2.
play_sequence.inputs_and_waits: _start_galaxy(); 30 process frames; finger 0 drag +30 px; finger 1 12 moves of +40 px, one frame per move.
